A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same DyT research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and matchable, including the relocated efficiency and batch-normalization studies.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results across vision, language, speech, and DNA tasks, plus ablations and batch-normalization replacement experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds compiled LLaMA 7B latency measurements in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The DyT formulation, normalization-replacement procedure, initialization prescriptions, and task-specific adaptations remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet-1K, The Pile and the same 15 language evaluation tasks, LibriSpeech, and human-genome/GenomicBenchmarks coverage. The compilation experiment adds an execution setting without changing datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: LN, RMSNorm, and BN remain the normalization comparators. Fixup, SkipInit, and σReparam remain in the corresponding method comparison, v1 Table 10/v2 Table 9. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix C adds torch.compile benchmarking, checking whole-model compilation and reporting timings with only DyT/RMSNorm layers compiled. The original 100-pass, 4096-token, H100/BF16 timing setup and existing training protocols are retained.

E4.justification: The added compiler-optimization control tests whether DyT's latency advantage persists after optimization. Existing squashing-function and α ablations, initialization sensitivity, training-stability analyses, and BN-replacement tests remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The timing measurements retain the same 100-pass aggregation, and the new compiled results introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing predictive results and unoptimized timings are retained. New Table 15 reports identical compiled timings for RMSNorm and DyT: 0.3/12.3 seconds for inference and 3.9/38.9 seconds for training, for layers/whole model over 100 passes. Whole-model compilation is reported to increase latency; v1's brief FP32 timing observation is omitted.

T1.justification: The normalization definitions and DyT equation remain unchanged, including Equations 1–2. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: v2 removes the Introduction's preliminary claim that DyT improves training and inference speed. The central claims about replacing normalization and matching or exceeding normalized models' performance remain unchanged in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: Section 9 newly acknowledges the absence of speedup after compilation/optimization and uncertainty across hardware and deployment environments. Appendix C adds conditional explanations about reduction bottlenecks and possible fusion optimizations. The existing mechanism interpretations and BN limitation are retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly identifies the original timing implementation as unoptimized Hugging Face LLaMA, adds its source reference, and documents torch.compile and compilation granularity. Existing training details in Appendix A and the project/code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hashemi et al. on harmonic/hyperbolic activation functions, Klambauer et al. on self-normalizing networks, and Jha and Reagen's AERO, plus a Hugging Face implementation reference. These modestly broaden context without substantially redefining DyT's positioning.

P1.justification: The efficiency subsection moves from Section 6.1 to Appendix C, and the previous Appendix C becomes D. The analysis introduction, related-work passages, and limitations receive localized edits; most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The original timing table moves from main-text Table 7 to Appendix C Table 14 with a clarified caption, and compiled-timing Table 15 is added. Minor figure formatting and page reflow accompany these changes; existing experimental displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The compiled comparison in Appendix C addresses an important qualification missing from v1's efficiency evidence: the reported speed advantage disappears under the tested optimization. Removing the introductory speed claim and explicitly stating this limitation improve the paper's reliability and practical interpretation. The gain is focused, while the method and broad empirical support remain unchanged.
